report:
The manuscript, discovery proof and supporting proofs n1–n4 establish the stated restricted singular-reference sufficient conditions. The regime is nonvacuous: F is continuous with q exp(F)/(2b)=H(x)>0, the singularity is the fixed logarithmic divisor plus a bounded continuous remainder, and the target residual Ω is uniformly positive. Approximation independence holds for the specified smooth positive residual forms converging uniformly as tensors while retaining the exact divisor.

The model and admissibility arguments check out. Invariance in the second factor reduces the envelope to the Kω₁ problem; rotation invariance is then used only for that reduced problem, so b need not be radial. The convex slope bound gives the stated exterior tangent line, and φ is an obstacle competitor once C≥C*. The bounded-type comparison establishes Pθ[φ]=φ. Matching first derivatives eliminates a boundary atom. The horizontal residual α=K·1_{|z|²<R}ω₁ has mass a, and the reference Monge–Ampère measure is 2bα∧ω₂, of positive finite mass. For λ/K<ε<1, ψ is an actual smaller-background competitor below φ. Finally, ddᶜθ≠0, and its invariance under smooth potential perturbations excludes the bounded Gauduchon case identified in the task.

Both Green-kernel normalizations construct the same mean-zero continuous w: adding 1 to the kernel changes nothing because A−a has mean zero. The bounds using kernel norms 1 and 2/e are both valid. Distributional differentiation yields ddᶜw=(A−a)ω₁. Off D, uniform mollification of the potential and its continuous complex Hessian identifies the recursive products with ordinary coefficientwise products. For the reference, the horizontal pullback current has square zero even at the cutoff circle. Removing the divisorial contribution therefore gives precisely Ω and Ω² for the solution, with Ω²=c exp(F)dV. All hypotheses for the task-granted scalar uniqueness and full-support nonemptiness have been established before use.

Multiplication is justified independently of supports: ρ=1/(2ab) is smooth and Ω is continuous. The horizontal summand of Q=ρΩ is closed distributionally because its coefficient depends only on the first factor; its other summand is constant. Consequently ddᶜQ=0 and ∫ρΩ²=1. The exact polynomial expansion for both signs of a small smooth potential perturbation proves D_uMA(h)=2Ω∧ddᶜh and L_uh=Δ₁h/A+Δ₂h/b. Stokes gives ∫L_uh dν=0 for ν=ρΩ².

The supporting-set argument uses the full C(X). The exact density curves F_t need not satisfy the factorization hypothesis, but their constructed solutions retain the reference type and scalar c. Scalar uniqueness gives Bφ(F_t)=Bφ(F); the supporting inequality for both signs of t forces every support to annihilate L_u. Nonemptiness subsequently establishes that the uniquely identified invariant probability satisfies the full supporting inequality.

Both signed-measure uniqueness proofs are valid. The heat argument constructs solutions of (Δ−V)f=g by a contraction with constant 1−min(V)/M<1. Heat smoothing approximates both f and its distributional Laplacian uniformly, so a finite signed annihilating measure vanishes without a regularity assumption. In n2, the logarithmic kernel first converts the measure equation into an L² density; only then is the spectral energy test applied. Parseval justifies the projections and passage to the limit, and positivity of V forces that density to vanish. Harmonic separation uses V=λ_kA/b>0 for every nonconstant mode. The constant mode gives the marginal, and uniform density of product tests determines every finite signed annihilator as C A dW. Probability normalization yields ν=(A/a)dW. A normalized nonnegative integrable weight defines an order-zero product with Ω and therefore equals ρ almost everywhere.

The approximation proof controls more than probabilities. Uniform residual convergence and determinant positivity imply F_j→F and L_jh→L_uh uniformly. Every subsequential adjoint-probability limit is stationary and hence equals ν. The uniformly convergent ratios (Ω_j∧ξ)/Ω_j² and dW/Ω_j² then establish convergence of the actual weighted currents and multiplier measures. No pointwise multiplier bounds or higher derivative bounds are assumed. Heat or rotation smoothing supplies a nonempty class; small mixed smooth perturbations supply nonsymmetric sequences. Normalizing potentials by constants changes none of these residual forms.

The example calculations are correct: mean A=1, εK−λ=3/8, target mass 4, reference mass 22/5, and height moments 0 and 5/24. The different reference and target masses cause no contradiction. For pole filling, the displayed density has integral one, equals 1/δ at p, and concentrates at p. The normalized adjoint limit assigns D mass 1/5; the weighted-current divisor coefficient is 1/10 in the numerical example. This verifies the stated obstruction to uncontrolled pole-filling recovery. Those sequences lose the fixed singularity type and uniform residual and density convergence, so the obstruction does not contradict the restricted theorem.

The indispensable external premises were checked in [Bedford–Taylor, §2](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf) and [Gauduchon, §3, Theorem 2 and its proof](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf). The former is applied locally to bounded psh products; the latter applies to every positive smooth residual metric on the connected compact surface, without the separate even-Betti hypothesis. Their ddᶜ conventions differ by the harmless positive factor 4π. Task-granted background is recorded separately below and excluded from external premises.

Two harmless wording clarifications suffice: measurable weight uniqueness means almost-everywhere uniqueness, as n2 explicitly states; “invariant probability” refers to L_u, while ρ is the adjoint weight for the measure-valued derivative. No substantial repair is needed. The result settles the singular-reference alternative only: it does not establish degenerate target residuals, arbitrary densities or singularities, arbitrary-potential uniqueness, or approximation independence from potential convergence alone.

passages.statement: On a ball U⊂C^N, for 1≤k≤N and locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions v₁,…,v_k, the Bedford–Taylor product ddᶜv₁∧⋯∧ddᶜv_k, defined recursively by ddᶜ(v₁ ddᶜv₂∧⋯∧ddᶜv_k), is a positive closed order-zero current, is symmetric and multilinear, and agrees with the smooth wedge product. It converges weakly when each factor is replaced by a decreasing sequence of locally bounded psh functions with a locally bounded psh pointwise limit. These assertions hold after rescaling to ddᶜ=i∂bar∂/(2π). (Bedford–Taylor, 1982, §2, equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.)

passages.statement: For every smooth strictly positive real (1,1)-form Γ on a connected compact complex surface, there exists a smooth strictly positive function r satisfying ddᶜ(rΓ)=0. The smooth real kernel of r↦ddᶜ(rΓ) is one-dimensional, so its positive solution is unique up to multiplication by a positive constant. This holds for ddᶜ=i∂bar∂/(2π). (Gauduchon, 1985, §3, Theorem 2 and its proof, Lemmas 1–2.)
passages.quote: Le noyau Ker L* est de dimension 1.

passages.quote: The standard admissible reference regime additionally requires a genuine envelope P_(epsilon theta)(phi) for some 0<epsilon<1. Then each bounded logarithmic density F has an ordinary-type solution MA_ext_theta(u)=c_phi(F)exp(F)dV with u~phi and scalar c_phi(F)>0 uniquely determined; potential uniqueness is not automatic.
